text: Findings are somewhat disparate when comparing changes in muscle development over time between ultrasound and MRI. A study involving 6 weeks of blood flow restriction training concluded that ultrasound measures of muscle thickness produced similar conclusions about hypertrophy as MRI-derived measures of cross-sectional area; however, the estimates of the magnitude of change were not equivalent (52). In another study, pre- to poststudy ultrasound-derived measures of vastus lateralis muscle thickness obtained at 50% of femur length showed a moderate to strong correlation with MRI-derived measures of ACSA ( r = .69) following 12 weeks of isokinetic resistance training for the knee extensors (32).
